name: Ma Tong Hyok

attribution.legal_posture: UN Panel-reported Member State allegation; publication records the response status as pending.

caveats: Money-laundering language is an allegation relayed by a Member State; the report's legal posture remains an allegation.
The Panel had not received a reply from Dalian Runguang at publication.

statements: A Member State alleged that Dalian-based manager Ma Tong Hyok brought Munitions Industry Department-subordinate IT workers to China and that Dalian Runguang knowingly worked with him and DPRK IT workers while laundering money for the DPRK.

sources.support: Supports the manager, company, worker-dispatch and laundering allegation, plus no-reply status

sources.quote: Ma Tong Hyok, allegedly a key information technology manager from the country based in Dalian who was directly involved in bringing information technology workers from the Democratic People’s Republic of Korea who are subordinate to the designated Munitions Industry Department to China.
According to the Member State, Mr. Ma and the teams of Democratic People’s Republic of Korea information technology workers under his oversight were in China as of late January 2020.

notes: Member State allegation relayed by the UN Panel; not an adjudicated finding. The late-January-2020 statement is historical and does not establish present location or current oversight.

identity_boundary: Ma Tong Hyok is preserved as the person named in a UN Panel report relaying a Member State allegation about an IT-management, worker-dispatch, and Dalian Runguang relationship. The report supplies a source-qualified allegation; UN designation, criminal charge, adjudication, current company role, present location, and same-named-public-account ownership remain unresolved.
